_about: Project settings for gallery_compare.py, kept out of the tool so the tool
can be copied verbatim.
CALIBRATE, DO NOT GUESS. Capture the same states twice without changing
anything, and diff the two captures. That is your noise floor. Set limits a
small multiple above it and record the measurement here, so the next person
knows whether a number is evidence or a guess.
If the noise floor is not near zero, something is non-deterministic and the
fix belongs in the capture harness, not in these numbers. Usual suspects:
animation driven by wall-clock instead of the sim clock, unseeded particle
systems, and effects drawn from the engine RNG (see GOTCHAS: a
non-deterministic call count cannot be fixed by a seed).
THREE criteria, because one is not enough. A whole-frame mean dilutes local
change: a band covering 3% of the screen, shifted by 40/255 and obvious to
any reviewer, averages to about 0.4 and slips under a mean-only gate. The
area criteria catch it.
mean          average absolute difference over all pixels, 0-255
changed_pct   percent of pixels differing by more than 2/255
strong_pct    percent of pixels differing by more than 32/255
Reference numbers from the project this kit came from: noise measured

overrides._format: state name -> partial limits, with the reason recorded here
overrides._warning: A state that cannot be reproduced is a harness bug worth fixing, not a threshold worth raising.

_calibration: Measured 2026-08-29 by capturing the set twice (tools/gallery.sh
--capture-only into two directories) and diffing:
boot_ready / boundary_skirt / countdown_go: 0.0000 / 0.000% / 0.000%
Limits stay at the kit's 0.50 / 1.00% / 0.10% - roughly 25x the worst
floor. Getting the floor here took three harness fixes, all recorded in
add-visual-conformance-gate: sim-tick-aligned driving (not loop
iterations), the same for the lap phases, and pausing the tree before the
settle frames so the sim cannot coast a run-varying tail.
Re-measured 2026-08-30 at M8 after adding graze_cones and fixing the
pre-race active camera (the world placeholder had held the viewport):
boot_ready / boundary_skirt / countdown_go / graze_cones: 0.0000 / 0.000% / 0.000%
boot_ready re-blessed deliberately: the old baseline was the placeholder
camera's view WITH the minimap disc visible over the kart (item 9 breach,
caught by the graze capture); the new one is the intended inspection pose.
Limits unchanged.
Re-measured 2026-08-30 at M9, after the boot world became the shipped
circuit and gate_next joined the set (tools/gallery.sh --capture-only into
two scratch directories, then gallery_compare.py between them):
boot_ready / boundary_skirt / countdown_go / graze_cones: 0.0000 / 0.000% / 0.000%
A bless-then-compare pass (two more captures) measured the same states at
(lap_banked) — the same order, still ~40x inside the limits, which stay at
0.50 / 1.00% / 0.10%. EVERY baseline was re-blessed at M9 and that is
expected, not drift: the world the game boots is now authored content with
six gates standing in it, and the HUD gained the GATE n/N line, the amended
hint text and the medal readout. gate_next is captured at tick 336, an exact
multiple of the 48-tick pulse period, so the next gate sits at full
gateNextColour rather than at whatever phase the frame caught.
Re-measured 2026-08-30 at M9 for rework-course-and-gate-direction, by
capturing the whole set twice into two scratch directories and diffing them
(gallery.sh --capture-only, then gallery_compare.py --current B --baseline A):
boot_ready / boundary_skirt / countdown_go / graze_cones: 0.0000 / 0.000% / 0.000%
gate_front / gate_back: 0.0000 / 0.000% / 0.000%
Limits unchanged at 0.50 / 1.00% / 0.10%. Note the tightest ratio honestly:
the mean and changed-area floors sit ~15x and ~5x inside their limits, but
strong_pct's worst state (hud_at_speed, 0.035%) is under 3x inside its 0.10%.
That is a small multiple rather than a comfortable one, and it is the number
to watch; it was not widened, because a tolerance is met, not moved.
EVERY baseline was re-blessed and that is expected, not drift: the shipped
course is a different seven-gate circuit, one prop fewer, and both gate marks
changed shape (the ground stripe is now an arrowhead along gate-forward and
the overhead chevron leads along it).
TWO STATES ARE NEW — gate_front and gate_back, tools/gate_side_capture.gd,
the same gate photographed from each side at tick 288. They are a pair on
purpose: the amended 'What a gate looks like' asks that a gate met from
behind read as the back of a gate, which is a comparison and cannot be judged
from one frame. Both measured a flat 0.0000 floor: nothing in them moves.
The blessed set was capture A; the compare above is capture B against it, so
the noise floor and the green compare are the same measurement.
